newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt profit up but shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt profit up but shares fall.

text.p: Austrian banking group Creditanstalt on Thursday reported a 10 percent rise in nine-month operating profit, roughly in line with market expectations, but its shares edged down in a weak stock market.

The bank, in the throes of a six-year long privatisation process, said operating profit in the January-September period rose to 4.65 billion schillings ($434 million), helped by a boost in its foreign subsidiaries.

Creditanstalt's preference shares were down 0.3 percent at 513 schillings, while its common stock was down 0.35 percent at 722.50. The ATX index of 21 blue chips was down 0.5 percent at 1,075.84 at the same time.
"The figures were at most slightly better than the market expected," said one trader.
But he added turnover on the Vienna market remained thin so that the news was unlikely to have a strong effect on the shares. "Right now, earnings just don't have much effect on the market," he said.
"It was a bit of a non-event," added another.
The bank's shares rose 0.7 percent on Wednesday in an otherwise limp Vienna market as investors sensed the bank's long-awaited privatisation neared.
This week, the finance ministry asked for renewed bids for its 70 percent voting stake in the bank to be in by November 15. ($1=10.72 Schilling)
